examples.ko: 그가 어제 한 말을 오늘 번복했어요.
examples.en: He reversed today what he said yesterday.

examples.ko: 한번 내린 결정을 번복하면 신뢰를 잃어요.
examples.en: If you reverse a decision once it's made, you lose trust.

examples.ko: 계약 직전에 조건을 번복해서 일정이 모두 틀어졌어요.
examples.en: The terms were changed right before the contract, so the whole schedule fell apart.

examples.ko: 증인이 진술을 번복하는 바람에 재판이 길어졌어요.
examples.en: The witness changed his statement, so the trial dragged on.
The company promised not to reverse its policy.
I have no intention of going back on my promise.

explain: 한 번 한 말, 결정, 약속, 판결을 뒤집을 때 써요. '바꾸다'보다 공식적이고, 신뢰를 잃게 한다는 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 '말을 바꾸다', '뒤집다'를 더 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 그는 어제 한 말을 또 번복했어요.
phrases.en: He took back what he said yesterday again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 한 말을 뒤집는 일에 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Very common for reversing something already said.

phrases.en: The first-trial ruling was reversed in the second trial.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a decision or ruling that was overturned.

phrases.en: Why did you suddenly reverse your decision?
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning, and more common in daily speech.

explain_en: It is used when you overturn something already said or decided, such as a statement, decision, promise or ruling. It is more formal than '바꾸다' and has a negative feeling of losing trust. In daily talk people more often say '말을 바꾸다' or '뒤집다'.

examples.en: A stenographer is seated in the courtroom.

examples.ko: 속기사는 말이 끝나는 대로 빠르게 받아 적어요.
examples.en: A stenographer writes down speech quickly as soon as it is spoken.

examples.ko: 제 꿈은 국회 속기사가 되는 거예요.
examples.en: My dream is to become a stenographer at the National Assembly.
I attend a training school to get a stenographer's license.

examples.ko: 속기사가 있어서 회의 내용이 정확하게 남아요.
examples.en: Because there is a stenographer, the meeting is recorded accurately.

examples.ko: 속기사에게 발언을 천천히 해 달라고 부탁받았어요.
examples.en: I was asked by the stenographer to speak more slowly.

explain: '속기사 자격증', '법원 속기사'처럼 써요. '속기'는 말을 빠르게 받아 적는 일을 가리켜서, 법정이나 국회처럼 기록이 중요한 곳에서 일하는 사람을 말할 때 많이 들어요.

phrases.en: I am studying to get a stenographer's license.
phrases.nuance_ko: 속기사가 되기 위한 자격 시험 이야기에서 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation used when talking about qualification exams for the job.

phrases.en: My friend works as a court stenographer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일하는 곳을 앞에 붙여서 어디서 일하는지 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting the workplace in front tells where the person works.

phrases.en: I want to become a stenographer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업을 목표로 말할 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic way to state this job as a goal.

explain_en: It is used in phrases like '속기사 자격증' and '법원 속기사'. '속기' refers to taking down speech quickly, so you hear this word about people working where records matter, such as courts and the National Assembly.

examples.en: As an aside, I heard the owner of that restaurant is a singer.

examples.ko: 강의 끝에 교수님이 여담을 하나 들려주셨어요.
examples.en: At the end of the lecture, the professor told us a little aside.

examples.ko: 여담으로 하나 더 말하면, 그 책은 영화로도 나왔어요.
examples.en: Just as a side note, that book was made into a movie too.

examples.ko: 회의 중에 여담이 길어져서 시간이 부족했어요.
examples.en: The side talk got long in the meeting, so we ran out of time.

examples.ko: 그 얘기는 여담이니까 안 들어도 괜찮아요.
examples.en: That story is just a side remark, so you don't have to listen.
Shall we stop the digression and get to the main point?

explain: 본론에서 벗어난 곁다리 이야기를 말하고, '여담이지만'처럼 말을 꺼낼 때 자주 써요. 영어의 gossip처럼 남의 소문을 말하는 뜻은 아니고, 가볍게 덧붙이는 이야기예요.

phrases.example: 여담으로 하나 더 말하면 이 책은 영화로도 나왔어요.
phrases.en: As an aside, this book was also made into a movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 본론이 끝난 뒤에 가볍게 덧붙일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to add a light extra remark after the main point is finished.

phrases.example: 딴 얘기지만 어제 본 영화 어땠어요?
phrases.en: Off topic, but how was the movie you saw yesterday?
phrases.nuance_ko: '여담이지만'과 비슷한 말인데 훨씬 편한 말투라서 일상 대화에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 여담이지만 but more casual, so it fits everyday conversation.

phrases.example: 여담이 너무 길어져서 수업이 늦게 끝났어요.
phrases.en: The digression went on too long, so class ended late.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곁다리 이야기가 너무 길어졌을 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a side story runs too long.

explain_en: It means a side story off the main topic and is often used to open a remark, as in '여담이지만'. It does not mean gossip about other people; it is a light extra story.

en: to be ended; to be finished

examples.en: The meeting wrapped up in an hour.
The long trial has finally come to an end.
When the case is closed, I will let you know the result.
I did not know it would end like this.
Please check the date when the lawsuit is concluded.

examples.ko: 싸움이 종결된 뒤에 모두 집으로 돌아갔어요.
examples.en: After the fight was over, everyone went home.

explain: '끝나다'와 같은 뜻이지만 딱딱해서 뉴스나 서류에 자주 나와요. 친구와 이야기할 때는 '끝나다'가 자연스러워요. 사람이 일부러 끝내면 '종결하다', 저절로 끝나면 '종결되다'를 써요.

phrases.en: We decided to end the meeting today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 일부러 끝낼 때 쓰는 능동형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form, used when someone ends something on purpose.

phrases.en: Class ends at three in the afternoon.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural than '종결되다' in everyday conversation.

phrases.en: The work has finally been wrapped up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이나 행사가 잘 정리되며 끝날 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when work or an event is neatly finished.

explain_en: Same idea as '끝나다' but stiff, so it appears in news and documents; with friends '끝나다' sounds more natural. When someone ends it on purpose use '종결하다'; when it just ends, '종결되다'.

examples.en: The company adopted my opinion.

examples.ko: 우리 학교는 새 교과서를 채택하기로 했어요.
examples.en: Our school decided to adopt a new textbook.
The president took the cheapest method.
If we adopt this method, costs go down.
Please tell me what the criteria for adopting are.
The answer the teacher chose was the correct one.

explain: 여러 안 중에서 하나를 골라 쓴다는 말이에요. '선택하다'가 개인 취향이나 일상에 어울리고, '채택하다'는 회의, 학교, 회사에서 방안을 정할 때 어울려요. 쓰는 사람은 힘 있는 쪽이에요.

phrases.en: The company adopted the best plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회의에서 여러 안 중에서 하나를 정할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for choosing one plan among several.

phrases.en: The school decided to adopt this textbook.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결정을 전할 때 자주 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common form for reporting a decision.

phrases.nuance_ko: 개인 취향이나 일상에서 고를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for personal taste and everyday choices.

explain_en: It means picking one option to use. '선택하다' fits personal preferences and daily life; '채택하다' fits meetings, schools and companies deciding on plans. The subject is usually the party with authority.

p.n: 선정하다 does not fit an opinion; 채택하다 means to adopt it.
